investigation.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-25T00:27–00:28Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurred at the very first network hop to the swarm backend, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents) returned a connection-level error before the production API could complete agent provisioning. This caused the production API to surface a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner, terminating the request after ~11 seconds with no agent identity or VM state produced. Because all three sibling checks share the same provisioning entry point and all carry the identical error message, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway or its upstream target, not to individual check logic or eval runner code.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The AWS ELB target group for the swarm provisioning service in us-east-2 had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — all backend instances were unhealthy, stopped, or the target group was empty, causing the load balancer to return 502.

[Likely] A transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production API and the ELB prevented the outbound connection from being established, producing the 'error sending request' message.
[Possible] The swarm provisioning service itself crashed or was restarted during the eval window, causing the ELB to return 502 while targets were cycling.
[Possible] A misconfiguration or deployment to the swarm provisioning service (e.g., wrong listener port, security group change, or target deregistration) rendered the ELB endpoint unreachable.

[Lower likelihood] The eval runner's access token or network egress path was blocked from reaching the ELB, though this is less consistent with the specific 'swarm gateway unreachable' error message returned by the production API itself.

investigations.summary: The eval-only check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 717 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, confirming this is an isolated snapshot-staleness failure, not a broad site or infrastructure outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 717 minutes (~11.95 hours). The contract requires the snapshot to be no older than 300 minutes (5 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid (all required evidence fields are present, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true), so the failure is exclusively a freshness violation caused by a missed or failed workflow execution, not a data-quality or schema problem.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed at the same run timestamp (2026-08-25T00:28:15–16Z), ruling out a shared infrastructure or site-wide failure.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot has not triggered or completed successfully within the last 717+ minutes, leaving the previously published snapshot stale. This is the primary cause supported by snapshotAgeMinutes=717 and source='github-actions' (failed-check.evidence).

Possible: The workflow was triggered but failed mid-run (e.g., a job error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) before writing a fresh snapshot, so the old artifact remains at the published URL.

Possible: A GitHub Actions scheduling gap — the workflow schedule may have been paused, disabled, or skipped (e.g., due to repository inactivity policies on GitHub Pages or Actions), causing no new run to complete in the expected window.

Less likely: A GitHub Pages CDN caching or propagation delay is serving a stale cached version of status.json even though a newer file was published. This is less likely given the magnitude of the age (717 min >> typical CDN TTLs) but cannot be fully excluded without inspecting the workflow run history.
